why: a `std::function` typedef, or the struct bundling one per event, that rclcpp hands to an entity's options. QoS events. rclcpp routes every event through one `set_on_new_qos_event_callback` plus a `QOSEventHandler` waitable the executor polls; ours are named callbacks per event registered on the entity -- five in C (`rclc_subscription_set_liveliness_changed_callback`, `rclc_subscription_set_requested_deadline_missed_callback`, `rclc_subscription_set_message_lost_callback`, `rclc_publisher_set_liveliness_lost_callback`, `rclc_publisher_set_offered_deadline_missed_callback`) and the same five in C++ (`Publisher::on_liveliness_lost`, `Publisher::on_offered_deadline_missed`, `Subscription::on_liveliness_changed`, `Subscription::on_requested_deadline_missed`, `Subscription::on_message_lost`). Constraint: no allocator for a per-event handler object and no wait-set to poll it from -- the C/C++ `(callback, context, entity)` triple lives in nros-c's process-wide `status_event_slots` table (16 registrations shared by C and C++, no allocator) and the backend is handed a generation-tagged slot reference, so a registration that outlives its entity is a no-op (issue 1993; until then the five Tier-1 C/C++ setters were UNSUPPORTED stubs that stored nothing). Whether an event is carried is the backend's answer: Cyclone DDS and zenoh carry all five, XRCE-DDS and uORB none, and there the setter returns UNSUPPORTED. The whole family was classified in the pubsub stage; see `cpp:QOSEventHandler`. A fn-ptr plus a `void *` context, not a `std::function`: no allocator for the closure's captured state.
